works.title: Enquiry — Of Cause and Effect
works.source: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (1748) · Project Gutenberg #9662 · public domain
works.note: His “sceptical doubts” — we never observe necessary connection, only constant conjunction. The problem of induction, stated for the first time.

works.section: In His Own Voice — Philosophy
works.title: Enquiry — Of Miracles
works.source: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (1748) · Project Gutenberg #9662 · public domain
works.note: No testimony suffices to establish a miracle unless its falsehood would be more miraculous than the event it reports.

works.section: In His Own Voice — Philosophy
works.title: Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion
works.source: David Hume, Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion (1779) · Project Gutenberg #4583 · public domain
works.note: His masterpiece on design and the problem of evil, in twelve parts. The sceptic Philo is usually taken to speak closest to Hume himself.

works.title: Alfred the Great
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part A · Project Gutenberg #19211 · public domain
works.note: A prince who “may with advantage be set in opposition to any monarch the annals of any nation can present.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Henry I
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part A · Project Gutenberg #19211 · public domain
works.note: Beauclerc, the scholar-king — learned and able, and not above seizing his brother’s crown.

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Henry II
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part A · Project Gutenberg #19211 · public domain
works.note: “The greatest prince of his time for wisdom, virtue, and abilities.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Richard I, the Lionheart
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part A · Project Gutenberg #19211 · public domain
works.note: All military genius and little else — “the most shining part of this prince’s character are his military talents.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: King John
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part A · Project Gutenberg #19211 · public domain
works.note: “Nothing but a complication of vices, equally mean and odious.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Richard III
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part B · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: The tyrant whose body was “in every particular no less deformed than his mind.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Henry VIII
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part C · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: “So different from himself in different parts of his reign” — a king the English admired even as he tyrannized over them.

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Elizabeth I
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part D · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: “Exposed to the calumny of enemies and the adulation of friends” — Hume weighs the great queen as sovereign and as woman.

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Mary, Queen of Scots
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part D · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: “A woman of great accomplishments… but unfortunate in her life, and during one period very unhappy in her conduct.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: The Duke of Buckingham
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part D · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: How a favourite is made and spoiled — loaded with honours till he was rendered “rash, precipitate, and insolent.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Charles I
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part E · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: Hume’s sympathetic portrait of the executed king — a prince of virtue, unsuited to his age.

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Oliver Cromwell
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part E · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: “Such violent ambition and such enraged fanaticism, with so much regard to justice and humanity.”

works.section: Portraits from the History of England
works.title: Charles II
works.source: David Hume, The History of England, Vol. I, Part F · Project Gutenberg · public domain
works.note: The easy, witty, faithless king — surveyed “in the different lights” of private man and public ruler.
